newsitem.title: USA: KKR, Xerox call off Talegen Holdings sale.
newsitem.headline: KKR, Xerox call off Talegen Holdings sale.

text.p: Xerox Corp and Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co have terminated an agreement under which Xerox was to sell its Talegen Holdings insurance business to investors led by KKR for $2.7 billion, the companies said Wednesday.
Xerox wants to sell the Talegen property and casualty insurance units as soon as possible, as it tries to exit the financial services business.
"Both parties worked hard and diligently to complete the transactions as originally envisioned," Paul Allaire, chairman and chief executive of Xerox, said in a statement.

"When it became clear that this could not be accomplished consistent with all the prevailing considerations of both parties, Xerox and KKR decided it was best to terminate the transactions," Allaire said.
KKR representatives declined to elaborate why the deal was cancelled or to comment on whether they would seek any other deals in the insurance business.
Xerox representatives were not immediately available for comment.

On January 18, Xerox and KKR reached agreements to sell the remaining Talegen and The Resolution Group units for a total of $2.7 billion to investor groups led by KKR and existing management. The consideration consisted of cash, securities, performance-based instruments and the assumption of Talegen debt.
In 1995 Xerox recorded a $1.5 billion charge related to the anticipated sales of Talegen and The Resolution Group. No additional charges are required as a result of the announcement Wednesday.
